Capture More Leads

Built for businesses that spend the day away from a computer — contractors, cleaners, landscapers. Every inquiry and missed call still gets answered.

The moment someone reaches out through your website, a text fires straight to your phone with their name and what they asked about. Speed wins jobs — most customers hire whoever answers first. Instead of an email sitting unread for hours, you’re calling them back while they’re still thinking about it.

When a call comes in and nobody can pick up, the caller instantly gets a friendly text letting them know you’ll get right back to them — and the conversation can continue right there by text. A missed call used to mean a lost customer who just dialed the next business. Now they get an answer in seconds, even after hours.

Local SEO

Most of this work is aimed at one thing: getting you found by people nearby who are ready to hire. That's your Google Business Profile, your presence in Maps and 'near me' searches, your reviews, and a website that clearly says what you do and the areas you serve. For a local service business, that's where the customers are.

Your Google Business Profile gets looked after every month — hours, services, photos, and posts kept current, so what customers find is always accurate. For most local businesses that listing is the real front door: it’s what shows up in Maps and 'near me' searches. A stale or wrong listing quietly sends customers somewhere else.

After a job well done, your customer gets a well-timed text asking for a review, with a direct link that makes it one tap. Reviews are the biggest reason strangers pick one local business over another — this turns asking from an awkward chore into an automatic habit that steadily builds the rating that gets you chosen.

Convert More Visitors

Turn visitors into booked appointments while you're busy working.

Customers pick an open time right on your website and it lands straight on your calendar, with confirmations and reminders sent automatically. People shop after hours — booking while the thought is hot beats a game of phone tag tomorrow, and the reminders mean fewer no-shows.

Why is my business not showing up on Google?

Usually one of a few fixable reasons. Your Google Business Profile may not be claimed or verified yet. Your business info — name, phone, hours, services — may be missing, wrong, or inconsistent across the web. Your website may not clearly say what you do and where you do it. Or competitors near you simply have stronger profiles and more reviews, so Google shows them first. And sometimes it’s just newness: a new business or website can take a while to get picked up. The fix starts with finding which of these it is — that’s the first thing we check.

How much does local SEO cost?

Honest answer: it depends. Your market, your competition, and how much work your online presence needs all change the number — a business in a quiet town needs less than one fighting ten competitors in a big city. That’s why there’s no generic price tag here: pricing is set on a quick call, after we’ve actually looked at your business, so you only pay for what you need.

How long does SEO take to work?

SEO is a build, not a switch. Most businesses start seeing movement in the first few months — showing up for more searches, more calls from Google — with stronger results building over three to six months and beyond. Anyone who promises you page one by next week isn’t being straight with you; Google doesn’t run on anyone’s schedule. What you get from us is steady work every month and a report showing exactly what changed.

What is local SEO?

It’s how a business gets found by people nearby who are ready to hire. When someone searches “plumber near me” or opens Google Maps, local SEO is what decides which businesses show up. It covers your Google Business Profile, your reviews, your website clearly stating your services and service areas, and your business information being consistent everywhere it appears online. Regular SEO is about the whole internet — local SEO is about your own backyard, where your customers actually are.

Is SEO worth it for a small business?

For most local service businesses, yes. Your customers are already on Google searching for exactly what you do, usually at the moment they need it. Showing up right then is the most valuable visibility there is — and unlike ads, it doesn’t stop the second you stop paying. The honest exception: if all your work comes from one referral source and you’re already booked solid, you may not need it. If you want the phone to ring more, this is where it comes from.

Can I do SEO myself?

The basics, yes — and you should. Claim and completely fill out your Google Business Profile, keep your hours and info accurate, ask happy customers for reviews, and make sure your website clearly lists your services and the areas you serve. Where it gets hard is the ongoing part: knowing which changes actually move the needle, doing them every month, and reading the data to adjust. Most owners would rather spend those hours on the work they’re paid for. That’s the part we take off your plate.

Do I need a website if I have a Facebook page?

Yes — they do different jobs. Facebook is great for staying in touch with people who already know you, but you don’t own it: your reach changes whenever Facebook feels like it, and people searching Google for a service near them mostly click businesses with real websites. Your website is the one place online you fully control — it shows up in Google search and Maps, takes inquiries and bookings around the clock, and makes you look established next to a competitor who only has a social page.
